block.txt: An Act to make provision for the issue of the New South Wales Photo Card; and for other purposes.
This Act is the Photo Card Act 2005.
This Act commences on a day or days to be appointed by proclamation.
In this Act—
authorised officer means—
a police officer, or
a person who is appointed for the time being by Transport for NSW as an authorised officer for the purposes of the provision in which the expression is used, or
a person (or a person belonging to a class or description of persons) prescribed by the regulations.
Photo Card means a New South Wales Photo Card issued under this Act.
photograph includes a digitised, electronic or computer generated image, and electronic data and other information used to create or generate a photograph.
Register means the Photo Card Register maintained by Transport for NSW under this Act.
Transport for NSW or TfNSW means Transport for NSW constituted under the Transport Administration Act 1988.
The Interpretation Act 1987 contains definitions and other provisions that affect the interpretation and application of this Act.
Notes included in this Act do not form part of this Act.

Transport for NSW has the function of administering the scheme established by this Act for the New South Wales Photo Card and has such other functions as are conferred or imposed by or under this Act.

heading.b: Photo Card to be issued by TfNSW

block.txt: Transport for NSW is to issue the New South Wales Photo Card as provided by this Act.
A Photo Card is to be in such form as Transport for NSW determines.

Transport for NSW may issue a digital Photo Card within the meaning of Part 2A to an applicant for a Photo Card only if the applicant has elected, whether at the time of the application or subsequently, to receive a digital Photo Card.
Transport for NSW may charge a fee prescribed by the regulations for the issue of a Photo Card.
A Photo Card is valid for the period for which it is issued, as determined by Transport for NSW and specified on the Photo Card.
A Photo Card is and remains the property of Transport for NSW.
The regulations may provide for—
the waiver or refund of fees payable for the issue of a Photo Card, or
the exemption of persons, or classes of persons, from the requirement to pay a fee for the issue of a Photo Card.
A person is eligible for the issue of a Photo Card only if Transport for NSW is satisfied that the person—
is ordinarily resident in this State, and
is at least 16 years of age, and
satisfies such other eligibility criteria as may be prescribed by the regulations.
A regulation for the purposes of subsection (1)(d) is not to be made except on the recommendation of the Minister made after consultation with the Attorney General.

heading.b: Grounds for refusal to issue Photo Card

block.txt: Transport for NSW must refuse to issue a Photo Card to a person if the person is not eligible for the issue of a Photo Card.

Transport for NSW may refuse to issue a Photo Card to a person if Transport for NSW is of the opinion that the person is not a fit and proper person to be in possession of a Photo Card because the person has been convicted of (or found guilty of or a guilty plea has been accepted for) any of the following offences—
an offence under this Act,
an offence involving fraud or dishonesty,
an offence prescribed by the regulations.
Transport for NSW may refuse to issue a Photo Card on such other grounds as may be prescribed by the regulations.
A regulation for the purposes of subsection (2)(c) or (3) is not to be made except on the recommendation of the Minister made after consultation with the Attorney General.

An application for the issue of a Photo Card is to be made to Transport for NSW in the form and manner required by Transport for NSW and supported by such information as Transport for NSW may reasonably require to establish or verify the eligibility, identity and residential address of the applicant.
An applicant for a Photo Card must provide a photograph of the applicant that is suitable for use on the Photo Card.
The applicant can provide the photograph only—
by authorising Transport for NSW to use any existing database photograph of the applicant that Transport for NSW determines to be suitable for use on a Photo Card to be issued to the applicant, or

if Transport for NSW determines that there is no existing database photograph of the applicant that is suitable, by having his or her photograph taken by Transport for NSW in accordance with arrangements made by Transport for NSW for the purpose.
In this section—

existing database photograph means a photograph of the applicant taken and kept by Transport for NSW in the exercise of any function under this Act, the Road Transport Act 2013, the Licensing and Registration (Uniform Procedures) Act 2002 or any other Act.

heading.b: Inclusion of other identity verification information on Photo Card

block.txt: Transport for NSW may include on or otherwise as part of a Photo Card any identifying information about the person to whom the Photo Card is to be issued (in addition to a photograph of the person) that Transport for NSW considers necessary or useful for verifying the identity of the person to whom the Photo Card is issued.
An applicant for a Photo Card must provide, in the manner determined by Transport for NSW, any information that Transport for NSW decides to include under this section.
Transport for NSW may cancel a Photo Card issued to a person by notice in writing to the person on any of the following grounds—
the person is not eligible for the issue of a Photo Card,
the Photo Card was issued in error,
the photograph on the Photo Card is no longer a true likeness of the person,
the Photo Card is incorrect in any respect,
such other grounds as may be prescribed by the regulations.
Transport for NSW may, by the notice cancelling a Photo Card or by subsequent notice in writing to the person, direct the person to return a cancelled Photo Card to Transport for NSW.

A person who is given a direction under this section to return a Photo Card must return the Photo Card to Transport for NSW within 14 days after the direction is given or such longer period as the direction may allow.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
Transport for NSW may decide to cancel a person’s Photo Card under this section without the person having been provided an opportunity to show cause why the Photo Card should not be cancelled.

If a person’s Photo Card is cancelled under this section, Transport for NSW may refuse to issue the person with any further Photo Card for such reasonable period as Transport for NSW may determine and specify in a notice served on the person by Transport for NSW.

heading.b: Damaged, lost, stolen or destroyed Photo Cards

block.txt: The person to whom a Photo Card has been issued must notify Transport for NSW as soon as practicable if the Photo Card is damaged, stolen, lost or destroyed during the period for which the Photo Card is valid.
Maximum penalty—10 penalty units.

heading.b: Administrative review of decision to refuse or cancel Photo Card

block.txt: A person aggrieved by a decision of Transport for NSW to refuse to issue or to cancel a Photo Card may apply to the Civil and Administrative Tribunal for an administrative review under the Administrative Decisions Review Act 1997 of the decision.
In this Part—
digital Photo Card means a Photo Card issued electronically using information (including a photograph) from the Register that—
is displayed on a mobile phone or other electronic device by way of software approved for that purpose by both the Secretary and Transport for NSW, and
includes any information required under this Act or the regulations to be included in a Photo Card.
relevant purpose, in relation to the use of a digital Photo Card, means any of the following—
complying with a request to produce an evidence of age document within the meaning of the Liquor Act 2007,
providing evidence of a person’s name or address for any purpose under the Registered Clubs Act 1976,
any other purpose prescribed by the regulations.
Secretary means the Secretary of the Department of Finance, Services and Innovation.
The holder of a digital Photo Card may use the digital Photo Card for a relevant purpose by displaying the digital Photo Card on a mobile phone or other electronic device.

Despite any other provision of this section, a person who displays or purports to display a digital Photo Card is not required to give or hand over, to the person who is requiring the Photo Card to be produced or handed over, the mobile phone or other electronic device on which the digital Photo Card is displayed or purported to be displayed.
If the holder of a digital Photo Card uses the digital Photo Card for a relevant purpose, the digital Photo Card is to be treated as if it were a Photo Card for that purpose.
A digital Photo Card is not displayed for the purposes of this section if—

the screen of the mobile phone or other electronic device on which it is purportedly displayed is unable to be read by the person to whom it is displayed due to cracking, dimming, dirt or any other fault, damage or obstruction, or

the holder of the digital Photo Card fails or refuses to comply with a reasonable request by the person to whom it is purported to be displayed to facilitate the reading, copying or scanning of the whole or any part of the digital Photo Card, or
the holder of the digital Photo Card refuses to comply with a reasonable direction to refresh the display of the Photo Card.

The holder of a digital Photo Card must remove the digital Photo Card from each mobile phone or other electronic device on which the digital Photo Card is capable of being displayed as soon as practicable after the holder is required to surrender or return the holder’s Photo Card.

A person who fails or refuses to remove the digital Photo Card from each mobile phone or other electronic device on which the digital Photo Card is capable of being displayed is taken to have failed to comply with the requirement to surrender or return the holder’s Photo Card.
A person removes a digital Photo Card from a mobile phone or other electronic device if the person updates the digital Photo Card in accordance with the directions of Transport for NSW.
Any requirement under this or any other Act or law to surrender or return a Photo Card does not extend to any mobile phone or other electronic device on which a digital Photo Card is displayed.

heading.b: Release or use of information for digital Photo Card

block.txt: Despite Part 4, Transport for NSW may—
use information, including photographs, in the Register for the purpose of exercising its functions, including delegated functions, or
release information, including photographs, in the Register if the release of the information is for the purposes of—
the issue of a digital Photo Card, or
the use of a digital Photo Card, or
verifying the authenticity of a digital Photo Card.
Transport for NSW is to maintain a Photo Card Register in the form of, or as part of, one or more computer databases or in such other form as Transport for NSW considers appropriate.
The following matters are to be recorded in the Register in respect of each person who holds a Photo Card—
the identification number allocated to the person to whom the Photo Card was issued,
the full name of the person (and any former name),
the person’s gender and date of birth,
the person’s residential address and address for service of notices (if any),
the commencement and expiry date of the period for which the Photo Card is valid,
such other information as Transport for NSW may include on or otherwise as part of a Photo Card.
Transport for NSW may record in the Register other information for—
the purposes of this Act or the regulations, or
the purposes of another Act, or
other purposes, as Transport for NSW considers appropriate.
Transport for NSW may correct any mistake or error in, or omission of, matter recorded in the Register.
The Register may be kept as part of or in conjunction with any register kept by Transport for NSW under the Road Transport Act 2013.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to requiring notice to be given to Transport for NSW of a change of address or other particulars in respect of a person to whom a Photo Card has been issued.

Transport for NSW must ensure that information contained in the Register that is of a personal nature or that has commercial sensitivity for the person about whom it is kept is not released or used except as provided by the regulations or under another law.

If there are reasonable grounds for believing that information contained in the Register is inaccurate or misleading, Transport for NSW may by written notice require the holder of a Photo Card to provide evidence to Transport for NSW, in a form specified by Transport for NSW, relating to anything relevant to the issuing of the Photo Card, including—
the holder’s personal details, and
the holder’s residential address.
For the purposes of this section, Transport for NSW may require the holder of a Photo Card—
to provide specified documents for inspection, and
to attend at a reasonable time and place specified by Transport for NSW for identification.

If a person who is required to attend for identification requests a change to the time or place specified in the notice, Transport for NSW must give consideration to that request and may change the time or place in accordance with the request.
A person who fails without reasonable excuse to comply with a requirement imposed under this section is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

heading.b: Photographs to which this Part applies

block.txt: This Part applies to photographs taken or provided in relation to applications for the issue of a Photo Card.

heading.b: Purposes for which photographs may be kept and used

block.txt: A photograph to which this Part applies may be kept and used by Transport for NSW only for one or more of the following purposes—
to reproduce the likeness of a person on a Photo Card,
to assist in determining the identity of any person in the course of determining whether or not to issue or replace a Photo Card,

in connection with an investigation relating to or leading to criminal proceedings against a person under any provision of this Act or under a provision of Part 4AA (Fraud) or 4AB (Identity offences), Division 2 or 3 of Part 5 (Forgery) or Part 5A (False and misleading information) of the Crimes Act 1900 in relation to a Photo Card,
for the conduct of criminal proceedings under this Act,
any purpose for which a photograph to which Part 3.5 (Protection of stored photographs) of the Road Transport Act 2013 applies may be kept and used by Transport for NSW under that Part,

any purpose for which a photograph to which Division 3 (Security and protection of photographs) of Part 4A of the Licensing and Registration (Uniform Procedures) Act 2002 applies may be kept and used by Transport for NSW under that Division,
for any other purpose prescribed by the regulations.
A photograph may be used for a purpose set out in this section at the time that the photograph is provided or taken or at any later time.
Transport for NSW must ensure that a photograph to which this Part applies is not released except—
to the NSW Police Force, or
to a driver licensing authority of another State or Territory, or

for the purpose of the conduct of any criminal proceedings under this Act or under a provision of Part 4AA (Fraud) or 4AB (Identity offences), Division 2 or 3 of Part 5 (Forgery) or Part 5A (False and misleading information) of the Crimes Act 1900 in relation to a Photo Card, or
to the Sheriff, for the purpose of any fine recovery proceedings, or
as provided under any other law, or
to the person whose likeness is shown in the photograph or on the database, or
as authorised or required under Part 3.5 (Protection of stored photographs) of the Road Transport Act 2013 in respect of the release of photographs to which that Part applies, or

as authorised or required under Division 3 (Security and protection of photographs) of Part 4A of the Licensing and Registration (Uniform Procedures) Act 2002 in respect of the release of photographs to which that Division applies, or
in accordance with the regulations.
Any release authorised by subsection (1)(a)–(d), or authorised by regulations made under subsection (1)(i), must be in accordance with any protocol approved by the Privacy Commissioner.

heading.b: Obtaining Photo Card by false statements

block.txt: A person must not—
by a false statement or any misrepresentation or other dishonest means, obtain or attempt to obtain a Photo Card, or
without lawful authority or reasonable excuse, possess a Photo Card obtained using those means.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A Photo Card obtained in contravention of this section is void, and Transport for NSW may alter the Register accordingly.
A person must not have in his or her possession without lawful authority or reasonable excuse—
a Photo Card, or
any article resembling a Photo Card and calculated to deceive.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person must not make a false document that could reasonably be taken to be a Photo Card with the intent that the document be used by any person as a Photo Card.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A person (the offender) must not give to another person a false document that could reasonably be taken to be a Photo Card with the intent that the document be used by any person as a Photo Card, if the offender knows or could reasonably be expected to know that the document is false.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person is guilty of an offence under this subsection if the person commits an offence under subsection (1) or (2) in circumstances of aggravation.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
For the purposes of this section, a person commits an offence in circumstances of aggravation if—
the offence involved a high degree of planning, or
the offence involved the use of other people acting at the direction of the person convicted of the offence in the commission of the offence, or
the person committed the offence solely or principally for financial reward, or

the offender has a previous conviction for an offence under this section, under clause 18 of Schedule 1 to the Liquor Act 2007 or under section 117EB (Manufacturing false proof of age cards) of the Liquor Act 1982.
A person must not give or lend the person’s Photo Card to another person if the person giving or lending the Photo Card knows or could reasonably be expected to know that the Photo Card may be used—
by the person to whom the Photo Card was given or lent, or by any other person, to provide proof of his or her age or identity, or
to obtain a Photo Card for the person to whom the Photo Card was given or lent, or any other person.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person must not fraudulently use or allow another person to use a Photo Card.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.
A person must not use a Photo Card—
that the person knows has been forged, fraudulently altered or altered in a manner that is calculated to deceive, or obtained by a false statement or misrepresentation or other dishonest means, or
that the person knows has been cancelled.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
In this section, use a Photo Card means use the Photo Card as proof of age or identity.

heading.b: Altering or tampering with Photo Card

block.txt: A person must not forge or fraudulently alter a Photo Card or alter a Photo Card in a way that is calculated to deceive.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
A person must not for an improper purpose wilfully or negligently alter, deface, or otherwise interfere with a Photo Card or with any of the material particulars contained on the Photo Card.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A person employed or engaged in connection with any aspect of the production of Photo Cards, or otherwise concerned in the administration of this Act or the regulations, who, otherwise than in the administration of this Act or the Road Transport Act 2013 or the statutory rules under those Acts—
reproduces, by photographic or other means, the likeness of a person that is depicted, or is to be depicted, on a Photo Card, or
causes or permits another person to do so,
is guilty of an offence.
Maximum penalty—50 penalty units.

The regulations may make provision for or with respect to expired Photo Cards (that is, Photo Cards that are no longer valid because the period for which they were issued has expired), including provision for or with respect to any of the following—
regulating or prohibiting the use for any or specified purposes of an expired Photo Card,
regulating or prohibiting the possession of an expired Photo Card,
requiring the surrender to Transport for NSW of an expired Photo Card,
requiring notice to be given to Transport for NSW if an expired Photo Card is damaged, stolen, lost or destroyed,
authorising the confiscation by an authorised officer of an expired Photo Card.

An authorised officer may direct a person who is in possession of a Photo Card, or thing resembling a Photo Card, to produce the Photo Card or thing to the officer if the officer reasonably suspects that the Photo Card or thing—
is not the person’s Photo Card or contains information that is false or misleading as to that person’s age or identity, or
has been forged or fraudulently altered or altered in a way that is calculated to deceive, or obtained by a false statement or misrepresentation or other dishonest means, or
is being used in contravention of any provision of this or any other Act or law.
A person must comply with a direction given to the person under this section.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.

A person is not guilty of an offence of failing to comply with a direction under this section unless the person was warned by the authorised officer when the direction was given that a failure to comply is an offence.

An authorised officer to whom a Photo Card, or thing resembling a Photo Card, is produced by a person representing it to be the person’s Photo Card or in response to a direction under section 28 may, with no authority other than this section, seize the Photo Card or thing if the officer reasonably suspects that the Photo Card or thing—
is not the person’s Photo Card or contains information that is false or misleading as to that person’s age or identity, or
has been forged or fraudulently altered or altered in a way that is calculated to deceive, or obtained by a false statement or misrepresentation or other dishonest means, or
is being used in contravention of any provision of this or any other Act or law.

A Photo Card or thing seized under this section is to be forwarded to Transport for NSW. Transport for NSW must cause the Photo Card or thing to be returned (by delivery or by post) to the person who produced it unless subsection (3) applies.
Transport for NSW may retain possession of and deal with a Photo Card or thing forwarded to Transport for NSW in such manner as Transport for NSW thinks fit if satisfied that the Photo Card or thing—
is not the Photo Card of the person from whom it was seized or contains information that is false or misleading as to that person’s age or identity, or
has been forged or fraudulently altered or altered in a way that is calculated to deceive, or obtained by a false statement or misrepresentation or other dishonest means, or
is being used in contravention of any provision of this or any other Act or law.

The authority conferred by this section to seize a Photo Card, or thing resembling a Photo Card, does not extend to a mobile phone or other electronic device on which a digital Photo Card within the meaning of Part 2A is displayed. This subsection does not limit any authority to seize a mobile phone or other electronic device conferred by any other law.

heading.b: Unauthorised demand for production of Photo Card

block.txt: A person must not, in connection with the supply of goods or services by the person, demand production by another person of that other person’s Photo Card.
Maximum penalty—20 penalty units.
This section does not prohibit a request for production of a Photo Card—
as a means of evidencing the identity or age of a person where it is reasonable for the person making the request to require evidence of the other person’s identity or age, or
where the person making the request is authorised by law to require its production.

For the purposes of this section, the making of a statement that could reasonably be understood, by a person to whom the statement is made, as indicating that the person is being required to produce his or her Photo Card is taken to be a demand for its production.
Transport for NSW may delegate the exercise of any function of Transport for NSW under this Act (other than this power of delegation) to—
any member of staff of Transport for NSW, or
any person, or any class of persons, authorised for the purposes of this section by the regulations.
Nothing in this section affects any other power of delegation that Transport for NSW has under any other Act.
An individual does not incur civil liability for an act or omission done honestly and in good faith in the course of his or her duties under this Act.

A liability that would, apart from subsection (1), attach to an individual because of an act or omission done honestly and in good faith in the course of his or her duties attaches instead to Transport for NSW.

Transport for NSW is not liable for any loss or damage resulting from the fraudulent or other improper use of a Photo Card (or thing that resembles a Photo Card) unless the liability results from the negligence of Transport for NSW or a member of staff of Transport for NSW. This subsection extends to a liability that attaches to Transport for NSW under subsection (2).
An amount of any unpaid fees or charges payable under this Act or the regulations is a debt due to Transport for NSW and may be recovered in a court of competent jurisdiction.
An authorised officer may issue a penalty notice to a person if it appears to the officer that the person has committed a penalty notice offence.
A penalty notice offence is an offence against this Act or the regulations that is prescribed by the regulations as a penalty notice offence.
The Fines Act 1996 applies to a penalty notice issued under this section.

The Fines Act 1996 provides that, if a person issued with a penalty notice does not wish to have the matter determined by a court, the person may pay the amount specified in the notice and is not liable to any further proceedings for the alleged offence.

The amount payable under a penalty notice issued under this section is the amount prescribed for the alleged offence by the regulations (not exceeding the maximum amount of penalty that could be imposed for the offence by a court).
This section does not limit the operation of any other provision of, or made under, this or any other Act relating to proceedings that may be taken in respect of offences.
Proceedings for an offence under this Act or the regulations may be dealt with summarily before the Local Court.

The Governor may make regulations, not inconsistent with this Act, for or with respect to any matter that by this Act is required or permitted to be prescribed or that is necessary or convenient to be prescribed for carrying out or giving effect to this Act.
The regulations may create offences punishable by a penalty not exceeding 20 penalty units.
Schedule 1 has effect.
The Minister is to review this Act to determine whether the policy objectives of the Act remain valid and whether the terms of the Act remain appropriate for securing those objectives.
The review is to be undertaken as soon as possible after the period of 5 years from the date of assent to this Act.
A report on the outcome of the review is to be tabled in each House of Parliament within 12 months after the end of the period of 5 years.
(Section 37)
The regulations may contain provisions of a savings or transitional nature consequent on the enactment of the following Acts—
this Act
Any such provision may, if the regulations so provide, take effect from the date of assent to the Act concerned or a later date.
To the extent to which any such provision takes effect from a date that is earlier than the date of its publication in the Gazette, the provision does not operate so as—
to affect, in a manner prejudicial to any person (other than the State or an authority of the State), the rights of that person existing before the date of its publication, or
to impose liabilities on any person (other than the State or an authority of the State) in respect of anything done or omitted to be done before the date of its publication.
